Surah 109, verses 1–6

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–6} That is: say to the disbelievers, openly and plainly: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾; that is, I disavow what you used to worship besides Allah, outwardly and inwardly. ﴿Nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾, because you are not sincere in your worship of Allah; so your worship of Him, when it is coupled with shirk, is not called worship. He repeated this so that the first (statement) would indicate the non-existence of the act, and the second would indicate that this has become a fixed attribute of them. For this reason he distinguished between the two groups and separated the two parties, saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, each acts according to his manner﴾ (17:84). You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do.
